body.answer_text: To push through a payment held by sanctions screening, re-key it on the LoanDesk backup screen [1]. The amount field comes pre-filled with zeros, so make sure to delete them before typing the correct amount [1].

memory.text: To push through a payment held by sanctions screening, re-key it on the LoanDesk backup screen. The amount field there comes pre-filled with zeros: delete them before typing the amount.

sources.transcript: When a payment gets held by sanctions screening and compliance tells you to push it through by hand, you re-key it on the LoanDesk backup screen. Almost nobody uses that screen, so nobody remembers this: the amount field comes pre-filled with zeros. Delete them before you type the amount. The approvers will look right past it, because the screen looks completely normal.

If LedgerOne is down, first contact the payments ops duty manager [1]. If the outage lasts more than 30 minutes, then call the LedgerOne vendor hotline [1].

memory.text: On-call escalation: payments ops duty manager first, then the LedgerOne vendor hotline if the outage lasts more than 30 minutes.

sources.transcript: On-call escalation goes to the payments ops duty manager first, then to the LedgerOne vendor hotline if it's still down after thirty minutes. The hotline is useless before then.

memory.text: The LedgerOne reconciliation report is wrong on the first business day of each month because of a timezone bug. Rerun it after 10 a.m. Eastern.

sources.transcript: The reconciliation report from LedgerOne is always wrong on the first business day of the month, because of a timezone bug. Rerun it after ten a.m. Eastern and it comes out right.
